analysis:
This PR is CI-only plus docs and a changelog. It adds a CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off gate to actions/cache restore and save steps across the composite actions (provider-ci-build and provider-release-build) and the workflows (ci-master, desktop, landing, provider-release-cache, provider-tests). The gate is set only on darkbloom-* runners with no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL, and the step writes only a constant to GITHUB_ENV, so no attacker-controlled data reaches it. It also replaces the 'Discard a damaged cached .git' step with one that rejects a restored .git that is a symlink or non-directory, holds symlinks or non-sample hooks, or whose config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include. It then runs git fsck. scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py is updated to pin both behaviors.

I confirmed from the integration replay (ci-master.yml, both composite actions) that the gate step precedes every cache step. The save steps carry the same gate as the restores, so a skipped restore cannot lead to a save under an unvalidated key. Release builds still revalidate the metallib and source timestamps after a restore, so cached content is not trusted blindly. No provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, key, App Attest or prefix-cache code changed, so A-001 to A-020, the TB-002 to TB-014 boundaries and T-041 are unaffected. Both changes narrow the CI cache-poisoning surface relevant to the signed-artifact chain (T-034, T-054, A-011, A-017).

Residual observations, not filed because they are hardening gaps in the new check rather than regressions, and the base had no equivalent check: the .git config check is a denylist. It does not screen filter.*, core.sshCommand, credential.helper or diff.external, and it inspects only files named config or config.worktree. Exploiting this needs a poisoned master-scoped cache write first, and PRs cannot save caches (SAVE_CACHES).

Unverified because the units were truncated or not supplied: the full head text of the later provider-tests.yml jobs, desktop.yml, landing.yml, provider-release-cache.yml, the provider-tests.yml composite action calls, and the DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL and runner-name contract. The tests only pin the YAML, so a later pass should confirm every cache step in the unseen ranges carries the gate and the new .git check.
